overview: Two fundamentally different ways electric current can flow — one keeps reversing direction, the other flows one way only.
genZNote: DC is a one-way street. AC keeps changing its mind, on schedule.

aspects.label: Direction of Flow
aspects.valueA: Periodically reverses direction (sinusoidal in most supplies).
aspects.valueB: Flows in one constant direction only.

aspects.label: Long-Distance Transmission
aspects.valueA: Easily stepped up/down via transformers for efficient long-distance transmission.
aspects.valueB: Cannot be transformed directly with simple transformers (requires conversion for efficient long-distance transmission).

aspects.label: How It's Measured
aspects.valueA: Described using RMS (root mean square) values, since instantaneous value constantly changes.
aspects.valueB: Described by a single constant value.
